project.name: Dart
project.summary: The Dart repository is an active shared foundation for SylphLab Dart and Flutter guidelines, Melos validation, and the sylph_lints package source.
goals: Own shared Dart and Flutter guidance under docs/.
Own the sylph_lints package source and Melos validation workflow.
Keep shared lint/style/testing rules tenant-neutral and safe for downstream projects to adopt.
nonGoals: Own downstream application behavior, app-store releases, or product-specific Flutter architecture.
Publish Dart packages until package release intent, publisher identity, and proof are documented.
Encode customer-specific rules into shared Dart guidelines.

owns.name: dart-guidelines
owns.description: Shared Dart and Flutter setup, style, quality, testing, documentation, and architecture guidelines under docs/.

owns.name: sylph-lints-source
owns.description: The sylph_lints package source, pubspec metadata, and Melos validation workflow.

doesNotOwn: Downstream application behavior, app-store releases, or product-specific Flutter architecture.
Enterprise doctrine, shared runner policy, or org-wide package release control.
Customer-specific lint/style rules unless they are generalized through documented shared guidance.
forbiddenCouplings: Do not add app-specific or customer-specific rules to shared Dart guidelines without a tenant-neutral rationale.
Do not publish sylph_lints until release intent, publisher identity, and publish proof are documented.
Do not rely on undocumented downstream assumptions when changing shared lint or style guidance.

delivery.deployPath: No deploy or package publish workflow is declared; CI validates formatting, analysis, and tests through Dart/Melos.
delivery.productionProof: Required CI context plus downstream package/guideline adoption evidence when consumers update.

gaps.description: CI is repo-local legacy GitHub Actions; migrate to central admission or stable status fan-in when the fleet workflow is ready.
Document whether sylph_lints should publish, and if so add release intent, publisher identity, required contexts, and publish proof.
